title: gRPC and Protobuf Stability: Evolution Playbook and CI Contracts
author: Asha Menon
content:
Summary
This playbook defines pragmatic, enforceable rules and CI checks for evolving gRPC services and Protobuf schemas used by Redwood Inference. It prioritizes backwards compatibility for SDKs and hosted APIs while enabling safe additive change and planned breaking migrations. The guidance applies to: internal microservices, public-facing Redwood APIs, and private deployment control-plane contracts.

Goals
- Keep client integrations working across minor releases (no silent breakages).
- Make schema changes reviewable and reversible via CI gates.
- Minimize runtime surprises by enforcing explicit deprecation and migration paths.
- Provide clear rollout recipes for both additive changes and controlled breaks.

Scope
This playbook covers: .proto design patterns, field numbering and reserved ranges, enum evolution, oneof/optional semantics, service method surface changes, error-code conventions for gRPC, CI tooling and tests, rollout playbooks, and observability requirements tied to schema changes. It does NOT replace API-level product decisions (e.g., removing features for product reasons) — those require a PRD and ADR.

Key Principles
1) Compatibility-first: Additive changes should be safe by default.
2) Explicit breaking changes: Breaking changes must be documented, gated by an ADR, and scheduled with a migration window.
3) CI-as-policy: Automated checks (lint, compatibility check, contract tests) are the primary enforcement mechanism.
4) Consumer-first testing: Every schema change must include at least one consumer-compatibility test (SDKs, internal services, or e2e harness).

Schema design rules (must-follow)
- Field numbers are immutable once used in a public contract. Reuse is forbidden. If a field is removed, immediately add its number to the message's "reserved" declaration. Example:

  message InferenceRequest {
    reserved 10, 11; // previous fields removed on 2025-09-21 ADR-123
    string prompt = 1;
    int32 max_tokens = 2;
    // ...
  }

- Never renumber. Never repurpose numbers.
- Use snake_case for field names. Keep names stable to aid debuggability.
- Prefer well-scoped nested messages to long flat messages (grouping improves additive changes).
- Avoid encoding opaque JSON blobs as text fields for core, versioned contracts. Use typed messages; if a flexible payload is required, use Any with an explicit registry table in docs.
- Default values: avoid relying on Protobuf default semantics in business logic. Always explicitly interpret presence where behavior differs for unset vs default.

Enum evolution
- Add new enum values only (numeric values must be unique).
- Never reassign numeric values.
- Reserve removed enum values via: reserved 5, 6;
- For enums that map to behavior with significant impact, add an explicit UNKNOWN/UNSPECIFIED value as 0 and require clients to handle it gracefully.

Oneof and optional usage
- oneof is allowed for mutually exclusive payloads, but consumers must ignore unknown oneof cases (server may receive unknowns from forward-deployed clients).
- optional (proto3) fields are permitted where presence semantics matter; code reviews must call out presence checks.

Service surface and methods
- Additive methods (new RPCs) are safe.
- Remove or rename an RPC is a breaking change and requires an ADR, compatibility tests, and a migration plan.
- For streaming RPCs, changes to message shapes used mid-stream are breaking — ensure staged rollout.

Error model and gRPC status mapping
- Standardize error payload: use a typed ErrorDetail message with machine-readable error_code, retryable flag, and human_message.
- Map common conditions to gRPC statuses consistently: e.g., INVALID_ARGUMENT -> 3, NOT_FOUND -> 5, UNAVAILABLE -> 14, INTERNAL -> 13. Include service-specific codes in ErrorDetail.error_code.

Versioning policy
- Three-tier policy: internal service contracts (semver-like, more agile), cross-team internal contracts (conservative), external/public APIs (strict).
- Service proto packages must include a package version namespace: package redwood.api.inference.v1;
- When a breaking change is required for a public API, create v2 package and namespace, keep v1 available for the migration window (minimum 90 days for public, 30 days for cross-team internal).

CI and tooling (required checks)
1) buf lint: enforce style and best practices (buf.yaml in repo). Command: buf lint --error-format=json
2) buf breaking: run against the live canonical artifact registry (see "Contract Registry" section) to validate non-breaking additions. Command: buf breaking --against .git#branch=main
3) contract tests: run the consumer-compatibility suite. This includes:
   - generated SDK smoke tests (python/node/go)
   - a light e2e integration run against a staging runtime that exercises the changed fields/methods
4) golden serialization tests: ensure wire encoding of messages remains compatible where expected.
5) schema-change PR template: every proto change must include: description, intended compatibility (additive|breaking), list of consumers, test artifacts, and rollout plan.

Contract Registry and artifacts
- Maintain a canonical proto artifact registry (buf registry or internal artifact bucket). All public/cross-team protos must be published for breaking checks to run.
- Release artifacts are immutable and tagged: redwood-protos:v2026-11-13. CI reads the registry URL from the environment: PROTO_REGISTRY_URL.

Rollout and migration playbook
For additive changes (common path):
1) Author change with full CI passing (lint + breaking=no + contract tests).
2) Merge to main and publish artifact to registry.
3) Deploy server with feature flag gating new behavior (default off for public APIs).
4) Enable opt-in consumers (internal teams can opt-in to test).
5) After 14 days and no regressions, accelerate rollout and remove flag if intended.

For controlled breaking changes (rare):
1) Open an ADR documenting rationale, migration plan, and rollback strategy. ADR must be approved by API owners and product.
2) Create vN namespace and implement tandem support for old and new services.
3) Publish migration SDKs and client shims.
4) Communicate schedule to consumers (minimum windows: public=90d, cross-team=30d, internal-service=7d).
5) Run consumers compatibility sweep and staged canary with percent-based rollout (0.5%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with automated rollback triggers on SLO regressions.

Staged canary and health gates
- Define health gates for each canary stage: 95th/99th latency, error rate, and token-cost-per-request. Example thresholds:
  - 95th latency increase < 10% relative to baseline
  - Error rate < 0.5% absolute increase
  - Token cost delta < 5%
- If any gate trips, abort and rollback automatically.

Observability requirements for schema changes
- Every proto change must add or update telemetry annotations in the message/service comment block (used by docs tooling) and add at least one metric or log trace point demonstrating the new field usage.
- Add a telemetry migration dash in Redwood Console: per-field ingestion sampling and SLI checks for the first 30 days after deployment.

Enforcement and exceptions
- CI checks are required for all PRs touching protos or generated clients. Failures block merge.
- Exceptions (e.g., emergency fix requiring a breaking change) require a signed-off exception ticket and post-hoc ADR.

Examples and snippets
- Reserving a removed field:

  message ModelMetadata {
    reserved 7; // removed experimental field on 2025-11-12
    string model_name = 1;
    repeated string tags = 2;
  }

- ErrorDetail example (proto):

  message ErrorDetail {
    int32 error_code = 1; // service-specific enum
    bool retryable = 2;
    string human_message = 3;
    map<string, string> metadata = 4;
  }

- buf CI snippet for GitHub Actions (example):

  name: proto-ci
  on: [push, pull_request]
  jobs:
    lint:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Install buf
          run: curl -sSL https://github.com/bufbuild/buf/releases/latest/download/buf-Linux-x86_64 -o /usr/local/bin/buf && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/buf
        - name: Lint
          run: buf lint --error-format=json
        - name: Breaking check
          run: buf breaking --against ${{ secrets.PROTO_REGISTRY_URL }}

Ownership and support
- API platform owners: eng-api-platform@redwood.internal (primary contact).
- Maintainers: teams owning proto packages must list a "proto steward" in the package README.
- On-call: for breaking changes that impact production, alert escalation follows the standard eng-sre oncall rota.

Appendix: Release note template (for schema changes)
- Title: [proto] <package> <message/method> change (additive|breaking)
- Preview: Short one-line summary
- Impact: Consumers affected, SDKs to bump, recommended migration steps
- Rollout plan: feature flag, canary schedule, rollback criteria
- Test matrix: list of compatibility tests that passed
- Owner: name, team, contact
